newsitem.title: USA: Smith Barney $250 mln debt deal postponed.
newsitem.headline: Smith Barney $250 mln debt deal postponed.

text.p: Smith Barney Holdings said its planned sale of $250 million of 10-year notes was postponed Wednesday.
"The deal has been postponed due to market conditions," a syndicate official at Smith Barney said.
Smith Barney is a unit of Travelers Group.
The debt offering was expected to price as early as Wednesday, and unofficial price talk on the deal was quoted at 60 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, dealers said.
Earlier, inflation warnings by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan triggered a multi-market selloff.
The benchmark U.S. Treasury bond sold off by over a point after the remarks and is currently trading off 36/32 at 98-15/32 to yield 6.74 percent, versus 6.65 percent at Tuesday's close.
In his remarks, Greenspan said financial markets, including stock and junk bond prices, may be overly optimistic about the economy. He urged caution.
